I've set up the Light Cycles project in `.planning/`, writing `PROJECT.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and `STATE.md`, and registered it in the cross-project portfolio. All 13 requirements (REQ-01 to REQ-13) and the out-of-scope list come straight from `TASK.md` and `docs/spec.md`; I didn't add any of my own.

The run was non-interactive and the project is set to autonomous mode, so I skipped the review step and kept the roadmap as drafted:

| # | Phase | Requirements | Plans | Personas |
|---|-------|--------------|-------|----------|
| 1 | Rules engine and test hook: a pure, self-contained rules module, the `window.tron` hook on a minimal page, a basic `chooseMove`, and `node --test` tests for every rule | 01, 03–06, 10, 12, 13 | 2 | engineering-senior-developer, testing-qa-verification-specialist |
| 2 | Playable browser game: canvas drawing, keyboard controls, the 15 ticks/s loop, the Space/P/round/match flow and the `#score`/`#message` text, checked with Playwright | 02, 07–09, 13 | 2 | engineering-frontend-developer, testing-qa-verification-specialist, design-ui-designer |
| 3 | Strong computer player: a set of test bots plus a script that plays the AI against them and reports win rates; tuning `chooseMove` to win as either player while staying under 20 ms per move | 10, 11, 13 | 3 | engineering-ai-engineer, testing-performance-benchmarker, engineering-senior-developer |

The repository has no code yet, so `/triad:map` isn't needed. Nothing is committed; that's up to you.

Next step: run `/triad:plan 1`.
